h1: The 5 Best Duplex Printers for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five printers with confirmed duplex printing for home offices, covering inkjet and laser, ADF scanning and running cost notes.
summary: The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is our best overall pick because it combines confirmed duplex printing with an automatic document feeder in the $50-100 bucket. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the laser choice for text-heavy volume. The Canon PIXMA TS6520 and TS4320 are the compact budget options.
intro: Duplex is one of those printer features that gets claimed loosely. Some listings say the printer can print two-sided when they mean you can flip pages by hand, and others only offer two-sided scanning. If you print contracts or reports, the difference decides whether paper bills shrink.

We reviewed eight printers and kept the five where the listing explicitly confirms duplex printing, leaving out three that do not. Ranking weighs duplex confirmation, document feeder, print technology, size, supplies and price bucket, from spec sheets and owner feedback rather than bench trials.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One with Duplex Printing
products.verdict: Confirmed duplex plus an automatic document feeder.
products.description:
The 8125e is a wireless all-in-one with confirmed duplex printing, an automatic document feeder and a three month Instant Ink trial. It also lists AI-capable printing features.

It ranks first because it combines two-sided printing with feeder scanning at the lowest of the bucket pairs. It sits in the $50-100 bucket, below the older 8125 listing.

It suits an office that scans stacks of paper. The caveat is that Instant Ink is a subscription after the trial.
products.idealFor: Home offices scanning and printing paper stacks.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer with Duplex
products.verdict: A compact monochrome laser for text-heavy volume.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a compact monochrome laser with confirmed duplex printing, copy and scan, a Refresh Subscription toner trial and Alexa support.

It ranks second because it is monochrome only and lacks the feeder listed on the HP, though laser suits high text volume. It sits in the $200-500 bucket, the highest of the group.

Best for contracts and reports. The caveat is that there is no color printing.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One with Duplex Printing
products.verdict: The same feature set as the 8125e at a higher bucket.
products.description:
This OfficeJet Pro 8125 lists confirmed duplex printing, an automatic document feeder, a three month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable printing features over wireless.

It ranks third because the specs match the 8125e, but this listing sits in the $100-200 bucket. If you find the e model, buy that instead.

It suits buyers who find this listing in stock. The caveat is the price difference with no obvious extra.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer with Duplex Printing
products.verdict: Compact color inkjet with a clear OLED status screen.
products.description:
The PIXMA TS6520 offers confirmed duplex printing, a 1.42 inch OLED display, a built-in copier and scanner and a compact body.

It ranks fourth because it has no automatic document feeder, unlike the HP models. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

It suits small desks that need two-sided color. The caveat is the manual scanning.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer for Duplex Printing
products.verdict: A plain compact duplex inkjet with a one-year warranty.
products.description:
The TS4320 lists confirmed duplex printing, a built-in copier and scanner, a compact single-tray design, a one-year limited warranty and easy setup.

It ranks last because it has no display or feeder, and a single tray limits paper types. It sits in the $50-100 bucket.

A reasonable choice for light two-sided printing. The caveat is the limited extras.
products.skipIf: You need a feeder or display.

whatMatters.detail: This means the printer flips the sheet itself to print both sides. Some printers only scan or copy two-sided. Look for duplex printing in the title or specs, not just two-sided copying.
Laser suits text and high volume, while inkjet handles color and photos. Monochrome laser cuts cost per page for documents. Choose based on what you print most.
An automatic document feeder scans a stack without lifting the lid each time. It saves time on contracts. Look for ADF in the listing.
Instant Ink and Refresh Subscription are monthly plans for ink or toner. They can lower cost but lock you in. Read the plan terms before enrolling.
Printers sit on desks, so depth and width matter. Compact models fit shelves. Check the dimensions against your space.

howToChoose.intro: How much you print decides laser versus inkjet.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Sharper text and cheaper pages for documents. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the laser pick.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Color and photos at a lower upfront price. The HP and Canon models are inkjets.

howToChoose.note: Most home offices should default to inkjet unless they print hundreds of text pages monthly.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Confirmed duplex, an automatic feeder and sharp text output.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The HP 8125e adds a feeder, while the Brother laser focuses on crisp text.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print text daily and want the Brother laser.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Printing is occasional, where the Canon TS4320 is enough.

faq.a: It is automatic printing on both sides of a sheet. The printer handles the flip, so you do not reinsert pages.
Not the same. Check the listing for duplex printing, not just two-sided copying.

faq.q: Is a subscription ink plan worth it?
faq.a: For frequent printing it can help. For occasional use, buying cartridges may cost less.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone?
faq.a: Most wireless models support mobile printing. Check the listing for the apps.

faq.q: How do I clean the print heads?
faq.a: Run the cleaning cycle from the settings menu. Do it only when prints show streaks.
Yes, because the sheet is flipped. For long documents the slowdown is small.

finalTake: The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the printer we would buy for a typical home office. Choose the Brother laser if you print text in volume, and a Canon PIXMA when space and price matter more. Check supply plans before you commit.
